archetype.name: Rebuilding (youth-first)
archetype.definition: A team that has finished near the bottom of the site's rankings in each of its last two seasons and is again built around young players who are getting big minutes before they can tilt the ice.

report.headline: The rebuild's shot share has gone backward, and the record is honest
report.take:
Chicago is 2-5-0, last in the Central, and 30th of 32 on the site's Teams tab. That is the same neighborhood as the last two seasons: 31st in 2024-25 and 30th in 2025-26. The question for a rebuilding team is not whether it wins in October. It is whether the underlying play is moving. Through seven games it is not. The 5-on-5 numbers have slipped: an xGF % of 37.8 (30th) and a CF % of 41 (31st), both below last year's 42.4 and 46.

The record is not a product of bad bounces. Pts vs Goal Diff sits at -0.3, essentially neutral, and the -12 goal differential matches a team being outshot and outchanced most nights. Special teams add to the problem. The power play converts 12.5% (28th) and the penalty kill 75% (24th), so Chicago is not stealing goals back when the game opens up. The forwards grade an F and the defense a D-, and the ice-time split shows why. The veterans eating minutes, Patrick Kane at -8 with a 35.9 xGF % and Bowen Byram at -7 in nearly 25 minutes a night, are getting buried rather than driving play.

The numbers hide some genuine signs of life among the young players. Anton Frondell leads the team with 6 points. Roman Kantserov has 3 goals and is the highest-ranked forward on his tab. Artyom Levshunov, at 74th of 239, is by a distance the best-rated defenseman on the roster. Two things argue that the goal totals are not wildly misleading either way. A PDO of 97.3 suggests some 5-on-5 shooting and save luck has gone against them. The goaltending, though, has been below average on the merits: Arvid Soderblom's .820 in two starts is the main reason the team GSAx is -4.1.

The direction looks like another season in the bottom four. Some puck luck should come back, and Spencer Knight is closer to average than his save percentage suggests. Neither fixes a team that controls only about two in five shot attempts. What matters is whether Frondell, Kantserov, Levshunov and Sam Rinzel take larger shares of the important minutes, and whether the 5-on-5 share climbs back toward last year's level. The win total will tell you little.

strengths.title: The kids are doing the scoring
strengths.body: The production that exists is coming from the young core. Frondell leads the team in points despite a 32.8 xGF %, and Kantserov's 3 goals lead the club and back up his rank of 47th of 110 on the right-wing tab. For a rebuilding team this matters more than the record. Whether it lasts depends on more of their shifts starting in the offensive zone, because right now they are scoring while being outchanced.

strengths.title: Levshunov is the one plus defenseman
strengths.body: On a blueline that grades D-, Levshunov ranks 74th of 239 at his position. His 44.6 xGF % is well clear of Byram, Vlasic and Kaiser in heavier or similar minutes. He already plays over 20 minutes a night, and his rating argues for more.

strengths.title: Knight has been near average
strengths.body: Knight's .885 save percentage looks poor, but his GSAx of -0.7 says he has been close to an average goalie given the chances he has faced. He ranks 30th of 64 on the goalie tab. The team's goaltending hole is mostly Soderblom's two starts, and last year's +7.5 team GSAx shows this position can be a positive.

concerns.title: Possession has regressed from last year
concerns.body: Chicago is getting 41% of 5-on-5 shot attempts and 37.8% of expected goals, both near the bottom of the league and both worse than the 46% and 42.4% of 2025-26. Seven games is a small sample. Still, a rebuild should be trending the other way, and it is a team-wide problem: only Ryan Greene is above a 50% xGF among regulars. If this holds for another month, it is the story of the season.

concerns.title: Opposing defensemen are feasting
concerns.body: Opposing defensemen are putting up 3.57 points a game against Chicago, 1.2 above what they normally produce, which ranks 29th. Their share of the points against is 31.3%, against a league norm of 24.8%. That points to forwards who are not getting out to the points and to long stretches pinned in the defensive zone. This is consistent with the shot-share numbers, so it is unlikely to be pure noise.

concerns.title: Veterans in big minutes are sinking
concerns.body: Byram plays a team-high 24.7 minutes and sits at -7, ranked 201st of 239 defensemen. Kane leads the forwards in ice time with a -8 and a -0.1 Game Score. Both groups' grades are weighted by ice time, so the F and D- partly reflect where the minutes are going.

trend.note: Steady at the bottom. The opening road trip went 0-3 with an 0-6 loss in Utah, and October has been a split of home wins over St. Louis and Pittsburgh around losses elsewhere, with the longest streaks just one win and three losses. Nothing in the shot or chance numbers suggests a turn yet.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games against special teams and a goalie wall
weekAhead.body:
Both games are at home, where Chicago has won twice. The opponents are hard in different ways. Winnipeg is 4-1-1 and 7th on the site, but its 5-on-5 play is mediocre (45.1 xGF %), and it leads the league in Pts vs Goal Diff. Even strength is where Chicago can stay close. The danger is special teams: the Jets' power play converts 31.3% and their penalty kill 92.3%, against a Chicago unit that is bottom-five on the power play and middling-to-poor on the kill.

Dallas is 2-3-1 and 22nd on the site, but its record undersells it. Dallas ranks 1st in goals against, carries an A+ goaltending grade and the league's second-best GSAx, and is last in Pts vs Goal Diff, so it has been unlucky. Its offense ranks 30th, so a low-scoring game is likely. A 104.6 PDO says Dallas's goaltending is running hot. Chicago needs Knight in net for both and cannot afford to chase.

keyMatchups.title: Chicago's special teams vs Winnipeg's
keyMatchups.body: Chicago's 12.5% power play runs into a 92.3% kill, and its 75% penalty kill faces a 31.3% power play. The Jets' record is padded by close-game luck, but special teams are a real edge for them here. Staying out of the box is Chicago's best path to a result.

keyMatchups.title: Young forwards vs the Dallas wall
keyMatchups.body: Dallas has held forwards furthest under their norms of any team but one and has allowed opposing defensemen just 1 point a game. Its goalies have saved 6.4 goals above expected. Frondell and Kantserov will be scoring against the stingiest setup they have seen.

keyMatchups.title: Winnipeg's luck vs Winnipeg's play
keyMatchups.body: The Jets' +2.1 Pts vs Goal Diff leads the league, while their xGF % ranks 26th. They are more beatable at 5-on-5 than their record suggests. Chicago will be outshot most nights, and a game like this one, against a team that is also getting outchanced, is where it can steal points.

weekAhead.watch: Chicago's 5-on-5 shot share against Winnipeg, a team that is also being outchanced. If the Blackhawks cannot get near even there, the possession slide is real.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a season close to the last two, which finished with 25 and 29 wins. The record so far is honest, with no close-game luck either way, so there is no big bounce owed. A sub-98 PDO should drift toward 100, and with Knight starting most nights, goals allowed per game should ease from above four. That is worth a few standings points, not a change in tier. Special teams at last year's level would help, since the power play converted 16.9% a year ago and the kill 83.6%.

The 5-on-5 share is the part that is not sustainable in a good way either. It is worse than last year's, and unless the young players drive it up, Chicago stays in the bottom four. For a rebuild, the meaningful outcomes are Frondell and Kantserov holding their scoring pace and Levshunov and Rinzel taking over the top defensive minutes.
swingFactors: Whether 5-on-5 shot share recovers toward last year's level
Knight taking the large majority of starts
Ice time shifting from the veterans to Frondell, Kantserov and Levshunov

confidence.note: Seven games is a small sample, but they match two years of history and shot data.
